text:
raj: CI is red for my PR - build succeeded but the image push stage keeps failing. error from build: "unexpected EOF while reading chunked body". pushing to registry.prod.redwood.ai:5000/redwood/service:pr-2389. anyone seen this exact EOF during push?

ci-bot: build #4821 failed: push step error -> unexpected EOF while reading chunked body

emma: have you tried a rerun? sometimes transient network flake. kicking a rerun now.

raj: rerun started (build #4822) - still failing with same EOF. paste of the push output below.

raj: ```
# buildctl output
[+] Building 34.1s (12/12) FINISHED
 => exporting to image
 => push to registry.prod.redwood.ai:5000/redwood/service:pr-2389
error: failed to upload blob: Put "https://registry.prod.redwood.ai:5000/v2/redwood/service/blobs/uploads/<uuid>?digest=sha256:...": net/http: HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
http: unexpected EOF
```

theo: two quick angles: 1) proxy/nginx truncation on chunked uploads, 2) corrupted/incomplete upload session on the registry side. can you share registry logs around the timestamp?

ops-bot: registry.prod logs (excerpt): 

```
2026-03-17T14:02:19Z INFO http: started PUT /v2/redwood/service/blobs/uploads/<uuid> from 10.42.3.128
2026-03-17T14:02:21Z ERROR http: connection reset by peer while reading chunked body
2026-03-17T14:02:21Z WARN  upload: aborting upload session <uuid> after client disconnect
```

lina: that stack looks like the reverse-proxy (nginx) closed the upstream connection mid-chunk. we saw a similar pattern last year when proxy_request_buffering was enabled combined with a strict client_max_body_size and an aggressive proxy_read_timeout.

kyle: also ask if this only fails on CI runners or locally for you too. raj: can you reproduce locally? try pushing from a dev laptop to rule out CI network path.

raj: I can reproduce locally from my laptop and also when I run the build in a k8s pod. tried both docker buildx and kaniko - both hit EOF during the final PUT. interestingly if I force smaller layers (split the large ADD), the push finishes.

emma: aha - that hints at a large single layer crossing some threshold. any recent Dockerfile change that adds a big tar or blob?

raj: yes — my PR added `ADD artifacts/dist.tar.gz /app/` (dist.tar.gz is ~420MB). previously we used `COPY` of smaller files.

theo: big single layer + proxy with buffering can cause the proxy to try to buffer the whole request and then hit client_max_body_size or memory/timeout. quick triage checklist:
- try `--no-cache` or `--squash` to reduce duplicated history
- test with smaller layer (you already saw it helps)
- check nginx conf: client_max_body_size, proxy_request_buffering off, proxy_read_timeout larger
- clear stale uploads on registry (there's an endpoint to list/delete aborted uploads)

lina: temporary mitigation: split the artifact into two smaller layers or extract the archive during build from a cached stage, so no single huge layer is uploaded. long term: ops should check proxy buffering flags and increase timeouts.

kyle: we can also flip the CI build to do an intermediate push with chunked transfer disabled if builder supports it. buildctl has options to tune upload parallelism. try: `buildctl build --frontend dockerfile.v0 --local context=. --local dockerfile=. --exporter image --opt push=true --opt upload.parallel=false` (if supported).

raj: trying a quick local repro: `tar -czf small.tar.gz <small subset> && ADD small.tar.gz /app` -> push succeeds. reverting to split archive helps.

emma: I'll do a bisect to find the exact commit that introduced the large artifact in the Dockerfile tree (likely my cleanup that consolidated assets). ping me if you need a patch revert in the meantime. bisect started. back in ~20.

ci-bot: build #4824 (after splitting layer) succeeded and push completed.

theo: conclusion: root cause = large single layer (dist.tar.gz ~420MB) triggering proxy/upstream to close chunked upload -> EOF. mitigation = split layer or adjust proxy settings. ops: can you log a follow-up to review nginx proxy buffering/timeouts in prod registry? tag @lina-ops and add runbook step to detect large-layer pushes.

lina: noted, filing ops ticket now and adding a monitor for consecutive EOF during uploads.

raj: thanks all — I'll update the PR to split the artifact and include a short note in the Dockerfile. :thumbsup:

emma: thanks for the quick help, team.
